title: Book Three · Chapter 159: The Two Places
story:
The winter holiday ends. Several weeks pass, and the first warm spring afternoons reach the school yard.

One day, Ronan and Anna stay beside the library steps after lunch. He has the coastal centre's picture. She has her notebook from the design visit.

Anna looks at the long worktable in his picture.

“You keep coming back to this one.”

“Yes. The longer lessons. The practice. English too.”

He turns the page toward her.

“I want to try a new place as well.”

She nods slowly. Then she opens her own notebook.

“I was excited in those rooms,” she says. “I was scared too. I have only seen one day there.”

“I feel scared about the coast,” Ronan says.

She moves her hand closer.

“I thought about living there,” she says. “After the visit.”

Ronan looks at the little shared room.

“Not only going for another day.”

“No.”

For a while, he can hear people talking near the library door. He watches one student carry a pile of books down the steps.

“I keep looking for one place for both of us,” he says.

Anna's fingers rest on her drawing.

“I keep looking for the right design course.”

He nods. He knows why she likes the work. He has watched her change a drawing again and again.

“I don't want to lose you.”

She looks up at him.

“I don't want that either.”

“I love you,” he says quietly.

Anna takes his hand.

“I love you too.”

He lets out a breath. She keeps her hand in his. The two pages still show different places.

“I wanted an easy answer,” he says.

Anna looks down at their hands.

“So did I.”

He almost says he can choose her city instead. The words are ready. Then he looks at the list of lessons in his own picture.

He has questions about those lessons because he wants them. Anna has spent months asking questions about different work.

“I can feel happy about your course,” he says. “And sad about the journey.”

“Yes.”

She holds his hand a little more firmly.

For a while, they watch people pass the library steps. A girl is telling her friend about a lost book. An older student goes inside with a full bag.

Their own next lesson will begin soon. Ronan does not want to spend every quiet minute counting the days until a departure.

Anna looks up at him again.

“We still have today.”

He nods. He wants the afternoons now, and the mornings after the journeys too. He begins to think about a way to keep both.

“Could we see each other every weekend?” he asks.

“We don't know the route between the cities yet.”

“Or the cost.”

She shakes her head. He looks at the coastal picture again.

“I still want to learn there.”

“I still want building design.”

Neither speaks for a few moments. Then Anna closes her notebook.

“We need to keep talking,” she says.

“And ask about the real journey.”

She nods. He folds his picture and puts it beside her bag while he finds his school book.

The bell rings inside. They stand and walk back across the yard together.

At their desk, Anna pulls her chair a little closer. Ronan puts the course page away and opens the next lesson.

Her sleeve touches his arm. He leaves his hand near hers until the teacher begins, then takes his pencil and looks toward the board.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

route＝路线；lose＝失去；as well＝也；either＝在否定句中表示“也”。

## 理解问题

1. 两人分别在寻找怎样的学习方向？为什么不能直接答应每周见面？
2. 这次是否宣布分手或同城终身保证？哪些具体动作和话表现仍相爱？

## 读句子

**She keeps her hand in his.**

拆开看：She / keeps her hand / in his.

她／把自己的手继续留着／握在他的手里。
